title: Appeals and Grievances Withdrawal and Refiling Rule
content:
**Withdrawing an Appeals and Grievances case**

A case is withdrawn only by the appellant's own confirmation: the agent records the request as an intake and the appellant confirms it. Withdrawal is possible only before a decision, where the tier allows withdrawal. A case that is filed or under review moves to withdrawn when the appellant confirms; the date of the confirmation is recorded as the date of the withdrawal.

A withdrawn case may be filed again under the tier's terms for filing again after withdrawal — only within the original filing deadline, which a withdrawal does not extend.

| Case status when withdrawal is asked for | Can it be withdrawn? |
|---|---|
| filed | yes, by the appellant's confirmation, where the tier allows withdrawal |
| under review | yes, by the appellant's confirmation, where the tier allows withdrawal |
| decided | no — withdrawal is possible only before a decision |

**Hypothetical timing.** A case on a tier with a 90-day filing deadline counted from a determination on day 0 is withdrawn on day 40. It may be filed again up to and including day 90; the 40 days that ran before the withdrawal are not added back.
